newsitem.title: ROMANIA: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 4 PM.
newsitem.headline: RADIO ROMANIA AFTERNOON HEADLINES AT 4 PM.

text.p: * The defence bugdet for 1997 will be approximately 2.0 percent of gross domestic product, which is insufficient to underpin the country's preparations to join NATO, Army Chief of Staff General Constantin Degeratu told a parliament commission.
Degeratu said Romania needs a minimum of $980 million to prepare for NATO admission.
* According to the budget draft, some $720 million have been earmarked for the army this year, said senator Radu Timofte, chairman of the Senate's standing defence commission.
* Parliament's finance commission heard National Bank (BNR) governor Mugur Isarescu on BNR's monetary policies following recent negotiations with international lenders.
He said the bank would absorb liquidities from the money market and cut the money supply which commercial banks use for hard currency trading.

* French President Jacques Chirac starts a two-day visit to Romania on Friday, accompanied by Foreign Minister Herve de Charette, Interior Minister Jean-Louis Debre and by Finance & Foreign Trade Minister Yves Galland, foreign ministry spokeswoman Gilda Lazar said.
French MPs and businessmen will also be part of Chirac's delegation, she said.
* Chirac will meet President Emil Constantinescu and Prime Minister Victor Ciorbea and address a session of parliament's two chambers.
* Debre and his Romanian counterpart Gavril Dejeu will sign a cooperation accord.
* A delegation of U.S. Senate advisers starts a three-day visit on Friday to evaluate criteria for Romania's NATO membership. -- Bucharest Newsroom 40-1 3120264
